idiom_name: nullable types with ?. / ?: and filterNotNull / mapNotNull / flatMap
implementation_notes: Kotlin puts nullability into the type system: String? and String are distinct, the compiler refuses to dereference a nullable without a check, ?. short-circuits to null and the Elvis operator ?: supplies a fallback, so the 0..1 focus needs no separate type. The plural traversal is standard-library collection processing: filterNotNull drops absent elements, mapNotNull maps and drops null results, and flatMap flattens nested collections in one pass. These operators and extension functions replace the classic optic structure; !! or a hand-written null check is only for values the compiler cannot smart-cast, and it gives up the guarantee.
pitfalls: The not-null assertion !! throws a NullPointerException exactly like an implicit Java dereference; it removes the compiler's evidence instead of handling absence.
Nullability does not survive Java interop: values from Java APIs are platform types that bypass the checks until the API is annotated.
mapNotNull silently drops elements whose transform returns null, which can hide a bug when null was never a legitimate outcome.
